proposals.after: On dingwei Li Shi, Director of the Imperial Household, became Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs; Bian Guidang moved from Vice Minister of Rites to Vice Minister of Justice; and Lu Jia from Vice Minister of Justice to Vice Minister of War.

proposals.before: On dingwei, Li Shi, Director of the Imperial Household, was made Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs; Bian Guichan, Vice Minister of Rites, was made Vice Minister of Justice; Lu Jia, Vice Minister of Justice, was made Vice Minister of War.
proposals.after: On dingwei, Li Shi, Director of the Imperial Household, was made Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs; Bian Guidang, Vice Minister of Rites, was made Vice Minister of Justice; Lu Jia, Vice Minister of Justice, was made Vice Minister of War.
proposals.reason: Same given-name error as in the idiomatic field: 歸讜 should be Guidang, not Guichan.

proposals.before: Liu Chong, Northern Capital garrison commander, Acting Grand Commandant, and Concurrent Councilor of the Second Rank, was also made military governor of Songzhou; and Shi Hongzhao, commander of the palace guard horse and foot and Concurrent Councilor of the Second Rank, was additionally promoted to Acting Grand Preceptor and Concurrent Palace Attendant;
proposals.after: Liu Chong, Northern Capital garrison commander, Acting Grand Commandant, and Concurrent Councilor of the Second Rank, was also made military governor of Songzhou; and Shi Hongzhao, commander of the palace guard horse and foot, Acting Grand Commandant, and Concurrent Councilor of the Second Rank—both were additionally promoted to Acting Grand Preceptor and Concurrent Palace Attendant;
proposals.reason: Chinese 並加檢校太師、兼侍中 applies to both Liu Chong and Shi Hongzhao; the idiomatic sentence wrongly attaches the final promotions only to Shi Hongzhao.

proposals.before: Liu Xin, military governor of Xuzhou, deputy commander of the palace guard, Acting Grand Commandant, and Concurrent Councilor of the Second Rank, was promoted to Acting Grand Preceptor.
proposals.after: Liu Xin, military governor of Xu Prefecture, deputy commander of the palace guard, Acting Grand Commandant, and Concurrent Councilor of the Second Rank, was promoted to Acting Grand Preceptor.
proposals.reason: Chinese 許州 is Xu Prefecture (Xuchang), not 徐州 Xuzhou; the English conflates the two.

proposals.before: Liu Zhu of Qingzhou and Murong Yanchao of Yanzhou, each Acting Grand Commandant and Concurrent Councilor of the Second Rank, were both promoted to Acting Grand Preceptor.
proposals.after: Liu Zhu of Qingzhou and Murong Yanchao of Yunzhou, each Acting Grand Commandant and Concurrent Councilor of the Second Rank, were both promoted to Acting Grand Preceptor.
proposals.reason: Chinese 鄆州 is Yunzhou; Yanzhou (兗州) is a different command already held by Fu Yanqing above.

proposals.before: Guo Congyi of Caozhou and Xue Huairang of Xingzhou were each promoted from Acting Grand Tutor to Acting Grand Commandant;
proposals.after: Guo Congyi of Chanzhou and Xue Huairang of Xingzhou were each promoted from Acting Grand Tutor to Acting Grand Commandant;
proposals.reason: Chinese 澶州 is Chanzhou; Caozhou is an incorrect place name.

proposals.before: Fu Yanqing, military governor of Yanzhou, Acting Grand Preceptor, Concurrent Palace Attendant, and Duke of Qi, was also made Concurrent Chief Councilor and enfeoffed as Duke of Wei;
proposals.after: Fu Yanqing, military governor of Yanzhou, Acting Grand Preceptor, Concurrent Palace Attendant, and Duke of Qi (岐), was also made Concurrent Chief Councilor and enfeoffed as Duke of Wei;
proposals.reason: Prior title 岐國公 (Duke of Qi as in Fengxiang Qi) is easily confused with 齊國公; mark the fief to avoid conflating with An Shenqi's new 齊國公.

proposals.before: Guo Jin, military governor of Huazhou and Acting Grand Commandant, was made military governor of Binzhou;
proposals.after: Guo Jin, military governor of Hua Prefecture (滑州) and Acting Grand Commandant, was made military governor of Binzhou;
proposals.reason: Chinese 滑州 is Hua Prefecture (Hua/滑), distinct from 華州 already rendered Huazhou; English 'Huazhou' conflates the two.

proposals.before: Bai Zairong, former acting governor of Zhenzhou and Acting Grand Tutor, was appointed military governor of Huazhou with the additional rank of Acting Grand Commandant;
proposals.after: Bai Zairong, former acting governor of Zhenzhou and Acting Grand Tutor, was appointed military governor of Hua Prefecture (滑州) with the additional rank of Acting Grand Commandant;
proposals.reason: Same 滑州/華州 conflation: Bai Zairong was appointed to 滑州 (Hua Prefecture), not 華州.

proposals.before: That same day Guo Congyi, military governor of Caozhou, was appointed overall commander of the Yongxing Army's horse and foot forces.

proposals.reason: Chinese 澶州 is Chanzhou; Caozhou is wrong (same error as earlier in the chapter).

proposals.before: On wuchen Li Hongxin, military governor of Suizhou and commander-in-chief of the Imperial Guard Cavalry, was made military governor of Cao Prefecture, and Guo Congyi, military governor of Cao Prefecture, was made military governor of the Yongxing Army and field headquarters commissioner.
